newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks ease on low institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks ease on low institutional buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Friday with most institutional buyers on the sidelines, and Chinese Lunar New Year holidays subduing activity, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.58 points down at 621.90. Price gains led declines by 20 to 16. Hayleys rose two rupees to 190, Development Finance fell five rupees to 275.

"Though the index has shown firm support at 620 points, it will be moving in a tight range on low turnover until Hong Kong, Colombo's main sorce of foreign investment, finishes Chinese New Year," said Shafi Waheed a trader at CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
Local institutions, meanwhile were testing the index's resilience, after profit-taking brought it down from about 630 points in late January, he said.

Turnover was 12 million rupees on 652,316 shares, supported by 103,700 Lanka Walltile, 105,600 Forbes Ceylon, 70,000 Vanik and 18,000 Grain Elevators. Foreign buying, led by Lanka Walltile, was 5.1 million rupees, and selling was 3.6 million.

"There is foreign buying of some finance and manufacturing stocks, which are expected to do better in 1997," said Deva Ellepola, a broker at Jardine Fleming. The two sectors were badly hit in 1996, by power cuts and a drought.
